group.passage: Most screens shine light straight into our eyes, but the screens inside many e-readers work in a very different way. Below, an engineering student explains how this technology, known as electronic paper, imitates ink on a printed page, and a lifelong book lover describes what happened when she finally gave it a try.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: How Electronic Paper Works
passage_parts.text: A printed page does not glow. It simply reflects the light around it, which is why a book is easy to read in a sunny park and impossible to read in a dark room. Electronic paper was designed to behave in exactly the same way. Its surface is covered with a layer of tiny capsules, each filled with a clear liquid in which white particles with a positive charge and black particles with a negative charge are floating. When a small voltage is applied beneath a capsule, one color is pulled up to the surface while the other sinks to the bottom, so every dot on the screen appears either black or white, just like ink on paper. Because the particles stay wherever they are placed, a page remains visible without using any power, and electricity is needed only when the image changes. As a result, many e-readers can last for weeks between charges. This clever design comes at a price, however: the particles move slowly, so the screen cannot play smooth video, and full color is still difficult to achieve.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Why I Finally Switched
passage_parts.text: For years I was skeptical of e-readers, sure that no screen could ever match the feel of a real book. A long train journey finally changed my mind. Reading on my phone, I found that the bright light made my eyes tired within an hour, yet the e-reader a friend lent me looked so much like a printed page that I soon forgot I was holding a machine. Since then I have read it at the beach in full sunshine and taken it on a week-long trip without packing a charger. Still, the switch has not been perfect. Every few pages the screen flashes black for a moment, and flipping back to find a passage I half remember is far slower than leafing through paper. I also miss small pleasures, such as the smell of an old paperback. So these days I keep both: the e-reader for travel, and paper books for the stories I want to live with.

translation_zh.text:
大多數螢幕把光直接照進我們的眼睛，但許多電子書閱讀器裡的螢幕運作方式非常不同。下面，一位工程系學生說明這種稱為「電子紙」的技術如何模仿印刷頁面上的墨水，一位一輩子愛書的讀者則描述她終於試用之後的經過。

A　電子紙如何運作
印刷的書頁不會發光。它只是反射周圍的光，這就是為什麼書在陽光充足的公園裡很好讀，在黑暗的房間裡卻完全沒辦法讀。電子紙的設計就是要以完全相同的方式運作。它的表面覆蓋著一層微小的膠囊，每顆膠囊裡都裝滿透明的液體，液體中漂浮著帶正電的白色粒子和帶負電的黑色粒子。當膠囊下方加上小小的電壓時，一種顏色會被拉到表面，另一種則沉到底部，所以螢幕上的每個點看起來不是黑就是白，就像紙上的墨水一樣。由於粒子會停留在被放置的位置，頁面不用耗電就能一直顯示，只有在畫面改變時才需要用電。因此，許多電子書閱讀器充一次電可以用上好幾個星期。不過，這個巧妙的設計是有代價的：粒子移動得很慢，所以螢幕無法播放流暢的影片，而且全彩顯示仍然很難做到。

B　我為什麼終於換了
多年來我一直對電子書閱讀器抱持懷疑，確信沒有任何螢幕比得上真正的書拿在手上的感覺。一趟長途火車旅行終於改變了我的想法。用手機閱讀時，我發現明亮的光不到一個小時就讓眼睛疲勞，但朋友借我的電子書閱讀器看起來太像印刷的書頁了，我很快就忘了自己拿著的是一台機器。從那之後，我曾在陽光普照的海灘上用它看書，也曾帶著它去旅行一個星期，連充電器都沒帶。不過，這次轉換並不完美。每翻幾頁，螢幕就會閃黑一下；想往回翻、找一段記不太清楚的文字，也比翻紙本書慢得多。我也懷念一些小小的樂趣，例如舊平裝書的氣味。所以現在我兩種都留著：電子書閱讀器用來旅行，紙本書則留給我想長久相伴的故事。
